angularDiameterSource: No angular diameter is measured: this is the record's radius at the Gaia distance.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 source 5864061893213196032: parallax 10.6124 +/- 0.0116 mas (RUWE 0.80), inverted to 94.2297 pc with no zero-point correction.
radiusSource: Temperature 4573 +/- 10 K, mass 1.00 +/- 0.02 solar masses and radius 1.01 +/- 0.02 solar radii as the ESO SupJup survey tabulates them (Zhang et al. 2024, arXiv:2409.16660, Table 1), from Bohn et al. (2020, ApJL 898, L16; arXiv:2007.10991) and Gaia: 702,657 km at 695,700 km per solar radius; GM from 1.00 solar masses times the JPL solar GM. Also catalogued as TYC 8998-760-1. presentationUp: the display axis (celestial north at the star) is up; no spin axis is measured on the sky.
effectiveTemperatureSource: 4573 +/- 10 K, as Zhang et al. (2024) tabulate from Bohn et al. (2020), https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.16660
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/yses-1.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.429, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius. The star's disc is not resolved; its colour is Gaia's spectrum of it.
